batch_node.name: rampart-20x-playground Placement Dimensions v0.2.0
batch_node.description: Four dimension axes as twenty dimension nodes: `actor` and `device` (customer, developer, administrator) and `column` and `row` (where a person or a computer stands on the Overview board). Placement hints for the landing view; no edges, the hierarchy is carried by the dotted name (req-dcom-naming). Each node carries `tap.meta: dimension` and no `dcom` value.

node.name: actor
node.description: Which kind of person an identity is, on the playground's landing view: `customer`, `developer` or `administrator`. The three values are the nodes named `actor.<value>`. An entity carries one value or none. The layout reads it to place people; it carries no access meaning.

node.name: actor.customer
node.description: The `customer` value on the actor axis: a customer of the system.

node.name: actor.developer
node.description: The `developer` value on the actor axis: a developer who builds and ships the system.

node.name: actor.administrator
node.description: The `administrator` value on the actor axis: an infrastructure administrator who operates the system.

node.name: device
node.description: Whose end-computing device a computer is, on the playground's landing view: `customer`, `developer` or `administrator`. The three values are the nodes named `device.<value>`. An entity carries one value or none. It is a separate axis from `actor` because a person and their computer are different things. The layout reads it to place devices; it carries no access meaning.

node.name: device.customer
node.description: The `customer` value on the device axis: the end-computing device of a customer of the system.

node.name: device.developer
node.description: The `developer` value on the device axis: the end-computing device of a developer who builds and ships the system.

node.name: device.administrator
node.description: The `administrator` value on the device axis: the end-computing device of an infrastructure administrator who operates the system.

node.name: column
node.description: Which column of the Overview board a person or a computer stands in, from the left: `0` to `5`. The six values are the nodes named `column.<value>`. An entity carries one value or none. A type with its own tagging system carries its column as a tag instead (`layout:column`). The layout reads it to place people and computers; it carries no access meaning.

node.name: column.0
node.description: The `0` value on the column axis: column 0 from the left of the Overview board.

node.name: column.1
node.description: The `1` value on the column axis: column 1 from the left of the Overview board.

node.name: column.2
node.description: The `2` value on the column axis: column 2 from the left of the Overview board.

node.name: column.3
node.description: The `3` value on the column axis: column 3 from the left of the Overview board.

node.name: column.4
node.description: The `4` value on the column axis: column 4 from the left of the Overview board.

node.name: column.5
node.description: The `5` value on the column axis: column 5 from the left of the Overview board.

node.name: row
node.description: Where a person or a computer stands within its column of the Overview board, from the top: `0` to `2`. The three values are the nodes named `row.<value>`. An entity carries one value or none. The layout reads it with `column`; it carries no access meaning.

node.name: row.0
node.description: The `0` value on the row axis: row 0 from the top of its column.

node.name: row.1
node.description: The `1` value on the row axis: row 1 from the top of its column.

node.name: row.2
node.description: The `2` value on the row axis: row 2 from the top of its column.
